## fetchRatifierInfo() function

Fetches maker bytecode and classifies the ratifier route for new offers.

The `bytecode` read is the result of `eth_getCode` for `params.maker` at the requested block. It is not returned to callers; it only tells the SDK whether the maker is an EOA or EIP-7702 account that can use Ecrecover signatures, or a deployed-code account that should use Setter root approval. Put the returned `ratifier` address on `Offer.create`<!-- -->, then use the returned `type` to choose `EcrecoverRatifierUtils.ratify` or `SetterRatifierUtils.ratify` after the tree has been built.

Reads `eth_chainId` only when the viem client has no configured chain id, then reads `eth_getCode` for `params.maker`<!-- -->.

**Signature:**

```typescript
export declare function fetchRatifierInfo(client: Client, params: {
    readonly maker: Address;
} & MidnightCallParameters): Promise<RatifierInfo>;
```

## Exceptions

`UnsupportedChainIdError` when no address registry exists for the client chain id.

`UnknownAddressError` when the registry has no configured ratifier address for the client chain id.

## Remarks

Parameter details:

- `params.maker`<!-- -->: Maker address whose bytecode determines the ratifier route.

- `params.blockNumber`<!-- -->: Optional block number used for the bytecode read.

- `params.blockTag`<!-- -->: Optional block tag used for the bytecode read.

## Example


```ts
import { fetchRatifierInfo } from "@morpho-org/midnight-sdk";

const maker = "0x7b093658BE7f90B63D7c359e8f408e503c2D9401";
const info = await fetchRatifierInfo(client, { maker });
// Pass info.ratifier to Offer.create(...), then use info.type after
// Tree.create([...]) to choose the Ecrecover or Setter ratifier flow.
console.log(info.type, info.ratifier);
```
